primary_claim: SAE-Rad, a framework that decomposes radiology-image class tokens into interpretable SAE features and generates reports from automatically-labeled active features, achieves competitive clinical accuracy versus state-of-the-art medical foundation models (outperforming CheXagent by up to 52% on CheXpert macro-F1-14, and reaching 92.1% / 89.9% of MAIRA-1 / MAIRA-2 performance respectively) while using a fraction of the parameter count and compute, and is claimed to be the first use of SAEs for a non-trivial downstream multimodal reasoning task.

effect.metric: CheXpert macro-F1-14 score (clinical relevance metric) relative to baselines
effect.value: outperforms CheXagent by up to 52%; reaches 92.1% and 89.9% of MAIRA-1 and MAIRA-2 performance respectively

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies prior VLM-based radiology-report-generation approaches (e.g. MAIRA) by arguing they require computationally expensive finetuning of multi-billion-parameter LLMs and may not be faithful to the underlying image-encoder's computations, whereas SAE-Rad avoids LLM finetuning and is interpretable by construction
limitations_stated: SAE-Rad underperforms on generic NLG metrics such as BLEU-4, which is expected since it does not optimize for a specific reference writing style
quote: Our method achieves competitive accuracy in comparison to state of the art medical foundation models while using a fraction of the parameter count and compute costs.
